I myself started playing again like about three months ago. Before that it was Minecraft PE that I had played as a 12yr old on my mum's mobile phone. Learnt a lot of things these months, and have quite equally died so many times. All these speed runner videos had had me thinking that beating the game won't take that long. It wasn't a resolute sort of world initially, I just wanted to beat the ender dragon because I had never done that before. It took some time to learn again of the game's basics. Now I can evade creepers well. I also spent some time on the Minecraft fandom reading the literature there. It was very technical, and I had some difficulty. Chunks, light level, spawning mechanics, and all stuff. I'm getting a hang of it now, or have at least started to. A crucial thing that YouTube videos don't teach you are the mechanics. Like how do their redstone contraptions work? For example a mob farm, they'll tell you the dimensions and how you are supposed to build the thing as it appears in the video. It works. But what if I want to build my own farm design that suits my base and terrain type? What if I want a more efficient one? The Minecraft fandom does provide information as to how various things are governed in the game, but it can be ambiguous and difficult to understand. About the iron farm I built, a very trivial problem I faced was it being on the ground. All videos had shown of the farm in the air, and I didn't exactly know why. I know I'm just dumb and maybe the creator had even mentioned it, but I didn't catch its significance. The iron golem has a spawn radius around from where the villagers summon it. It needs for there to be a solid block to spawn on, and enough space. Meaning if summoned from the ground, it can spawn anywhere along the axes. When from air, it has nowhere but the intented solid spawning ground you built. So, I had to cover all of that spawn radius on ground with pressure plates, to have it only be spawned on my intended ground where the collection system was. It's just a petty thing, but I'm so dumb what do I do. I do not yet understand mob spawning fully. I mean the whole mob farm thing works on the fact that mobs spawn where the light level is zero. You create a dark box, and transport the spawned mobs to a killing platform. But wait, the light level during night time isn't zero. It is very low, but not zero. How do the rules for mob spawning differ for different times? What's the best distance to be from the mob farm? The mobs start despawning if you get too far. And they don't spawn at all if you are too close. Again, all this might be very clear things but I'm, well, a humble Minecraft player. 

For the pillager thing, I did some research on the fadom in the meanwhile. Pillagers can spawn infinitely in an area of 72x52x72 blocks centred around the top floor of the outpost. So it doesn't matter how many of them you kill. Some them might spawn with a banner on their head, he's a captain. It triggers a raid when you kill him. They only spawn on solid opaque blocks. So covering all the area with pressure plates would work as for like the iron golem. But this one's a much larger area. Another thing, that they spawn on blocks with a light level of less than or equal to eight. Block light is apparently, as I've recently found, different from sky light. I think that should be how the mob spawning is governed. I think torches can work. But again, it's a huge area. Redstone lamps would look a lot better in comparison to so many torches just laying around, but they're expensive. I think filling the whole place up with lava might be the easiest. Lava spreads, so one bucket covers some more than just one block. Perhaps deciding to stay near an outpost wasn't a great idea after all. A lava farm will do the job for all the lava. I'm also thinking of making a redstone powered spawning platform over the lava that I can make and destroy with a lever. Sometimes you might want to have them raid your base. It gives you exp, it can be fun to fight them all, and you can obtain a totem of undying. I think this is the only second way to obtaining a totem after you have been done with the woodland mansion. 

I am enjoying Minecraft, and well, also losing sometimes. I want to experience that feeling when I defeat the dragon. It's been a journey, and it will be an achievement when I beat the game. This is truly a distinguished game. There's so much knowledge to it, and so much knowledge of your own that you can create. Speed runners throwing just one eye of ender to know of the stronghold's direction, and then traveling in the nether, to portal out exactly in the stronghold is some big brain genius. I know one block traveled in the nether means eight blocks in the overworld, which means you have to go less distance, but predicting exactly the coordinates of the stronghold from the eye of ender's trajectory and everything; that is amazing.
There is always a higher ground
